members.tone: The family's plain baseline - it says the thing has whatever draws love, without dressing the quality up as innocence or sweetness.
The full-spelt form, identical in warmth and force to *lovable*.
Superlative where *lovable* is merely descriptive - affection is not attracted but compelled, and the childlike or naive streak is what compels it.
Puts the effect in motion rather than the quality at rest: it wins affection over, where *adorable* simply announces the winning is done.
Broad, easy warmth for the same childlike appeal, without the surrender *adorable* implies.
Lifts sweetness to an ideal - praise that leaves no room for a fault in the nature described.
The extended form of *angelic*, reaching for the same unblemished sweetness with a more formal ring.
Takes the cherub rather than the angel: sweetness that is small, round and fond instead of exalted.
The most rarefied of the angel words - sweetness raised to something radiant and remote, well past the homely warmth of *cherubic*.
The unadorned name for the nature the angel words put wings on - the same quality with none of the exaltation.
Carries the invitation in its build - a thing that asks to be held, stated more deliberately than *cuddly*.
Soft, offhand and physical: the appeal is being huggable, not being good-natured as in *sweet*.
